patterns: Patterns across the 24 schools surveyed: every institution uses an instructor-discretion model for classroom AI rules rather than a single university-wide mandate, though defaults differ — several (Ohio State, Michigan State, Minnesota, Stanford, Harvard) treat unauthorized AI use as misconduct by default, while others simply require a syllabus statement. Canvas dominates the LMS market (20 of 24); Michigan State, Purdue, and USC use D2L Brightspace. Microsoft Copilot with enterprise data protection is the most common campus AI tool, with Google Gemini spreading rapidly in 2025-26. A smaller group has direct OpenAI deals (ASU first in Jan 2024, then UCLA, Illinois, Nebraska, USC, MIT); Michigan and Penn State built their own multi-model platforms instead. Minnesota's posture is mid-pack: licensed Gemini and Copilot but no OpenAI deal and no homegrown platform, with new central AI governance (Vice Provost for AI, AI Hub) arriving in 2026.
